token.description: The Qovery API Token to use. This can also be specified with the `QOVERY_API_TOKEN` environment variable. To generate a token, navigate to your [Qovery Console](https://console.qovery.com) > Settings > API Tokens.

block.description: The [Qovery](https://www.qovery.com/) provider is used to interact with the resources supported by Qovery. The provider needs to be configured with the proper credentials before it can be used.

annotations.description: Map of annotation key-value pairs to include in this group. Keys and values must conform to Kubernetes annotation constraints.

id.description: Unique identifier of the annotations group (UUID format).

name.description: Name of the annotations group. Must be unique within the organization.

organization_id.description: Id of the organization. **Cannot be changed after creation** (forces resource replacement).

scopes.description: Set of Kubernetes resource types to which these annotations will be applied. Valid values are: `PODS`, `DEPLOYMENTS`, `STATEFUL_SETS`, `SERVICES`, `INGRESS`, `HPA`, `SECRETS`, `JOBS`, `CRON_JOBS`.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery annotations group resource. This can be used to create and manage Qovery annotations groups.

Annotations groups allow you to define reusable sets of Kubernetes annotations at the organization level. These groups can then be attached to Qovery services (applications, containers, jobs, Helm charts) to automatically apply consistent Kubernetes annotations across your deployments. Unlike labels, annotations are scoped to specific Kubernetes resource types (e.g. pods, deployments, services).

advanced_settings_json.description: Advanced settings as JSON. Use `jsonencode()` to set values. Only include settings you want to override. Full list available in [Qovery API documentation](https://api-doc.qovery.com/#tag/Applications/operation/getDefaultApplicationAdvancedSettings).

annotations_group_ids.description: List of annotations group ids. Annotations groups allow you to add Kubernetes annotations to the application's pods.

arguments.description: List of arguments of this application. Overrides the Docker image's default `CMD`.

auto_deploy.description: Specify if the application will be automatically redeployed after receiving a new commit on the configured branch.

auto_preview.description: Specify if the environment preview option is activated or not for this application. When enabled, Qovery creates a preview environment for each pull request. Default: `false`.

cooldown_period_seconds.description: Period in seconds to wait after the last trigger before scaling back down. Defaults to 300.

polling_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds between each KEDA polling of the scalers. Defaults to 30.

config_json.description: Scaler configuration as JSON. Mutually exclusive with config_yaml.

config_yaml.description: Scaler configuration as raw YAML. Mutually exclusive with config_json.

enabled.description: Whether the scaler is enabled. Defaults to true.

role.description: Role of the scaler: PRIMARY or SAFETY.

scaler_type.description: Type of the KEDA scaler (e.g. cpu, memory, prometheus, cron).

trigger_authentication.description: Inline KEDA TriggerAuthentication for this scaler.

scalers.description: List of KEDA scalers driving the autoscaling. At least one scaler is required.

autoscaling.description: Event-driven autoscaling (KEDA) configuration. KEDA is additive to the CPU/memory HPA (min/max_running_instances) and unlocks scale-to-zero (min_running_instances = 0). Requires KEDA to be enabled on the cluster.

build_mode.description:
Build mode of the application.
  - `DOCKER`: Build using a Dockerfile in the repository. Requires `dockerfile_path` to be set.
  - `BUILDPACKS`: Build using Cloud Native Buildpacks (auto-detects language and framework).

Default: `DOCKER`.

value.description: Value of the environment variable.

built_in_environment_variables.description: List of built-in environment variables linked to this application. Built-in variables are automatically generated by Qovery and include host information, port mappings, and other service metadata. These are read-only and cannot be modified.

cpu.description: CPU of the application in millicores (m) [1000m = 1 CPU].

generate_certificate.description: Qovery will generate and manage a TLS/SSL certificate for this domain using Let's Encrypt.

use_cdn.description:
Indicates if the custom domain is behind a CDN (e.g. Cloudflare). This affects how Qovery validates the CNAME during deployment:
  - If `true`: Qovery only checks that the domain points to an IP.
  - If `false`: Qovery checks that the domain resolves to the correct service Load Balancer.

validation_domain.description: URL provided by Qovery. You must create a CNAME on your DNS provider using that URL.

custom_domains.description: List of custom domains linked to this application. You must configure a CNAME record on your DNS provider pointing to the `validation_domain` value.

mode.description: Restriction mode. `MATCH`: deploy only when changes match the value. `EXCLUDE`: deploy only when changes do NOT match the value.

type.description: Type of deployment restriction. Currently only `PATH` is supported.

value.description: Value of the deployment restriction (e.g. a file path pattern like `src/` or `services/api/`).

deployment_restrictions.description: List of deployment restrictions. Deployment restrictions allow you to control when an application is deployed based on file path changes in the git repository.

deployment_stage_id.description: Id of the deployment stage. Deployment stages allow you to control the order in which services are deployed within an environment.

docker_target_build_stage.description: The target build stage in a multi-stage Dockerfile to build. Only applicable when `build_mode = "DOCKER"` and using a multi-stage Dockerfile.

dockerfile_path.description: Path to the Dockerfile relative to the `git_repository.root_path`. Required when `build_mode = "DOCKER"`. Example: `Dockerfile` or `docker/Dockerfile.prod`.

entrypoint.description: Entrypoint of the application. Overrides the Docker image's default `ENTRYPOINT`.

environment_id.description: Id of the environment. Changing this forces the application to be re-created.

description.description: Description of the environment variable alias.

id.description: Id of the environment variable alias.

key.description: Name of the environment variable alias.

value.description: Name of the variable to alias.

environment_variable_aliases.description: List of environment variable aliases linked to this application.

description.description: Description of the environment variable file.

id.description: Id of the environment variable file.

key.description: Key of the environment variable file.

mount_path.description: Mount path of the environment variable file.

value.description: Value of the environment variable file.

environment_variable_files.description: List of environment variable files linked to this application.

description.description: Description of the environment variable override.

id.description: Id of the environment variable override.

key.description: Name of the environment variable override.

value.description: Value of the environment variable override.

environment_variable_overrides.description: List of environment variable overrides linked to this application.

value.description: Value of the environment variable.

environment_variables.description: List of environment variables linked to this application.

ephemeral_storage.description: Ephemeral storage of the application in GiB. When unset, the platform default is used.

external_host.description: The application external FQDN host. Only available if your application has at least one publicly accessible port.

description.description: Description of the external secret file.

id.description: Id of the external secret file.

key.description: Name of the external secret file.

mount_path.description: Absolute path where the secret file will be mounted inside the container.

reference.description: Reference to the upstream secret (e.g. the secret name or ARN in AWS Secrets Manager).

secret_manager_access_id.description: Id of the secret manager access to use for this external secret file.

external_secret_files.description: List of external secret files linked to this application. External secret files reference upstream secrets (e.g. from AWS Secrets Manager) and are mounted as files at a given path inside the container.

secret_manager_access_id.description: Id of the secret manager access to use for this external secret.

external_secrets.description: List of external secrets linked to this application. External secrets reference upstream secrets (e.g. from AWS Secrets Manager) via a secret manager access configuration.

branch.description: Branch of the git repository to use for builds. Defaults to `main` or `master` (depending on repository).

git_token_id.description: The git token ID to be used for authenticating with the git provider. Required for private repositories. Reference a `qovery_git_token` resource.

root_path.description: Root path of the application within the repository. Useful for monorepos where the application code is in a subdirectory. Defaults to `/`.

git_repository.description: Git repository configuration for the application source code.

failure_threshold.description: Number of consecutive failures required to declare the probe as failed.

initial_delay_seconds.description: Number of seconds to wait after the container starts before the first probe is executed. Use this to give your application time to initialize.

period_seconds.description: How often (in seconds) to perform the probe after the initial delay.

success_threshold.description: Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure.

timeout_seconds.description: Number of seconds after which the probe times out. If the probe does not respond within this time, it is considered failed.

command.description: The command and its arguments to execute (e.g. `["cat", "/tmp/healthy"]`).

exec.description: Exec probe: runs a command inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0. The command binary must be present in the container image.

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

service.description: The gRPC service name to health-check. If not specified, the overall server health is checked.

grpc.description: gRPC probe: checks that the given port responds to gRPC health check requests. The service must implement the [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/10/01/health-checking-grpc-servers-on-kubernetes/#introducing-grpc-health-probe).

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

scheme.description: Scheme to use for the HTTP request. Must be `HTTP` or `HTTPS`.

host.description: Optional host to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

readiness_probe.description: Configuration for the readiness probe, used to determine when your service is ready to receive traffic. If the readiness probe fails, the service is temporarily removed from the load balancer until it passes again.

healthchecks.description: Configuration for the healthchecks that are going to be executed against your service. At least one of `readiness_probe` or `liveness_probe` should be configured for production workloads.

icon_uri.description: Icon URI representing the application. Used in the Qovery console UI.

internal_host.description: The application internal host. Use this to communicate between services within the same environment.

is_skipped.description: If true, the service is excluded from environment-level bulk deployments while remaining assigned to its deployment stage.

labels_group_ids.description: List of labels group ids. Labels groups allow you to add Kubernetes labels to the application's pods.

max_running_instances.description: Maximum number of instances running for the application.

memory.description: RAM of the application in MB [1024MB = 1GB].

min_running_instances.description: Minimum number of instances running for the application.

external_port.description: External port of the application. Required if `ports.publicly_accessible = true`. Must be between 1 and 65535.

internal_port.description: Internal port of the application. Must be between 1 and 65535.

is_default.description: If this port will be used for the root domain. The API may override this value based on port configuration (e.g., when only one publicly accessible port exists, it will be set as default).

protocol.description: Protocol used for the port of the application.

publicly_accessible.description: Specify if the port is exposed to the world or not for this application.

ports.description: List of ports linked to this application. At least one port must be set as `publicly_accessible = true` with an `external_port` for the application to be reachable from the internet.

value.description: Name of the secret to alias.

secret_aliases.description: List of secret aliases linked to this application.

mount_path.description: Mount path of the secret file.

value.description: Value of the secret file.

secret_files.description: List of secret files linked to this application.

value.description: Value of the secret override. The value is write-only and will not be displayed in plan outputs.

secret_overrides.description: List of secret overrides linked to this application.

value.description: Value of the secret. The value is write-only and will not be displayed in plan outputs.

secrets.description: List of secrets linked to this application.

mount_point.description: Mount point of the storage for the application.

size.description: Size of the storage for the application in GB [1024MB = 1GB].

type.description: Type of the storage for the application.

storage.description: List of persistent storage volumes linked to this application. Data stored in these volumes persists across application restarts.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery application resource. This can be used to create and manage Qovery applications.

An application is a service built from source code in a git repository. Qovery builds the application using either Docker (with a Dockerfile) or Buildpacks, then deploys it to your cluster.

argocd_url.description: URL of the ArgoCD instance (e.g. https://argocd.example.com).

id.description: Unique identifier of the ArgoCD credentials.

block.description: Provides a Qovery ArgoCD credentials resource. This can be used to configure ArgoCD integration for a cluster.

agent_cluster_id.description: Id of the Qovery cluster where the ArgoCD instance is running.

argocd_cluster_url.description: URL of the ArgoCD destination cluster (e.g. https://kubernetes.default.svc).

cluster_id.description: Id of the Qovery cluster mapped to the ArgoCD destination.

id.description: Composite identifier of the mapping, matching the import format (organization_id,agent_cluster_id,argocd_cluster_url).

organization_id.description: Id of the organization.

block.description: Provides a Qovery ArgoCD destination cluster mapping resource. This maps an ArgoCD destination cluster URL to a Qovery cluster.

access_key_id.description: AWS IAM access key ID. Required when using access key authentication. Must not be set when `role_arn` is specified. Use a variable reference instead of hardcoding this value.

id.description: Unique identifier of the AWS credentials (UUID format).

name.description: Name of the AWS credentials. Used for display purposes in the Qovery console.

organization_id.description: ID of the Qovery organization in which to create the credentials. **Cannot be changed after creation** (forces resource replacement).

role_arn.description: ARN of the AWS IAM role that Qovery will assume (e.g., `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/QoveryRole`). Use this for cross-account access or when you prefer role-based authentication. Must not be set when `access_key_id`/`secret_access_key` are specified.

secret_access_key.description: AWS IAM secret access key. Required when using access key authentication. This is a sensitive value and will not be displayed in plan output. Use a variable reference instead of hardcoding this value.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery AWS credentials resource. This is used to create and manage AWS credentials that Qovery uses to provision and manage EKS clusters and associated resources in your AWS account.

You can authenticate using either **IAM access keys** (`access_key_id` + `secret_access_key`) or an **IAM role** (`role_arn`). These two methods are mutually exclusive.

advanced_settings_json.description: Advanced settings of the cluster as a JSON string. Use `jsonencode()` to set values. The complete list of available settings is in the [Qovery API documentation](https://api-doc.qovery.com/#tag/Clusters/operation/getDefaultClusterAdvancedSettings). Only include settings you want to override.

cloud_provider.description:
Cloud provider where the cluster will be deployed.

  - `AWS` - Amazon Web Services (EKS).
  - `GCP` - Google Cloud Platform (GKE).
  - `SCW` - Scaleway (Kapsule).
  - `AZURE` - Microsoft Azure (AKS).
  - `ON_PREMISE` - On-premise infrastructure.

credentials_id.description: ID of the cloud provider credentials to use for this cluster. Must match the `cloud_provider` type (e.g., use `qovery_aws_credentials.id` for AWS clusters, `qovery_gcp_credentials.id` for GCP clusters).

disk_size.description: Disk size of the cluster nodes in GB. The default value depends on the cloud provider and instance type.

aws_vpc_eks_id.description: The ID of the existing AWS VPC (e.g., `vpc-0123456789abcdef0`).

documentdb_subnets_zone_a_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone A for Amazon DocumentDB. These should be private subnets.

documentdb_subnets_zone_b_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone B for Amazon DocumentDB. These should be private subnets.

documentdb_subnets_zone_c_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone C for Amazon DocumentDB. These should be private subnets.

eks_create_nodes_in_private_subnet.description: Whether to create EKS worker nodes in private subnets. When `true`, nodes are not directly accessible from the internet and route traffic through a NAT Gateway.

eks_karpenter_fargate_subnets_zone_a_ids.description: List of private subnet IDs in availability zone A for EKS Fargate (required when using Karpenter). These subnets must be private and connected to the internet through a NAT Gateway.

eks_karpenter_fargate_subnets_zone_b_ids.description: List of private subnet IDs in availability zone B for EKS Fargate (required when using Karpenter). These subnets must be private and connected to the internet through a NAT Gateway.

eks_karpenter_fargate_subnets_zone_c_ids.description: List of private subnet IDs in availability zone C for EKS Fargate (required when using Karpenter). These subnets must be private and connected to the internet through a NAT Gateway.

eks_subnets_zone_a_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone A for EKS worker nodes. These subnets must have `map_public_ip_on_launch` set to `true`.

eks_subnets_zone_b_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone B for EKS worker nodes. These subnets must have `map_public_ip_on_launch` set to `true`.

eks_subnets_zone_c_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone C for EKS worker nodes. These subnets must have `map_public_ip_on_launch` set to `true`.

elasticache_subnets_zone_a_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone A for Amazon ElastiCache. These should be private subnets.

elasticache_subnets_zone_b_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone B for Amazon ElastiCache. These should be private subnets.

elasticache_subnets_zone_c_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone C for Amazon ElastiCache. These should be private subnets.

rds_subnets_zone_a_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone A for Amazon RDS databases. These should be private subnets.

rds_subnets_zone_b_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone B for Amazon RDS databases. These should be private subnets.

rds_subnets_zone_c_ids.description: List of subnet IDs in availability zone C for Amazon RDS databases. These should be private subnets.

existing_vpc.description:
AWS existing VPC configuration. Use this block to deploy the Qovery cluster into an existing AWS VPC instead of creating a new one. All EKS subnets are required, while database and cache subnets are optional.

~> **Warning:** This configuration cannot be changed after cluster creation.

additional_ip_range_pods_names.description: Additional secondary IP range names for pods. Use this when you need multiple pod IP ranges (e.g., for multi-tenancy or large clusters).

ip_range_pods_name.description: Name of the primary secondary IP range in the subnetwork to use for GKE pods.

ip_range_services_name.description: Name of the secondary IP range in the subnetwork to use for GKE services (ClusterIP range).

private_nodes.description: Make GKE nodes private with no public IPs. Node traffic goes through the gateway instead of exposing node public addresses.

subnetwork_name.description: Name of the GCP subnetwork within the VPC to use for the GKE cluster nodes.

vpc_name.description: Name of the existing GCP VPC network to use (e.g., `my-existing-vpc`).

vpc_project_id.description: GCP project ID that owns the VPC. If omitted, defaults to the project associated with your GCP credentials. Use this when the VPC is in a different project (Shared VPC pattern).

gcp_existing_vpc.description:
GCP existing VPC configuration. Use this block to deploy the Qovery GKE cluster into an existing Google Cloud VPC network instead of creating a new one.

~> **Warning:** This configuration cannot be changed after cluster creation.

gke_kms_key.description:
GCP KMS key resource name used to encrypt the GKE cluster's boot disks / etcd / storage buckets / volumes. Only supported on GCP clusters.

~> **Warning:** This value cannot be changed after cluster creation. You'll need to create another cluster.

default_service_architecture.description: Default CPU architecture for services deployed on this cluster. Common values: `AMD64`, `ARM64`. This determines the default node architecture when no specific architecture is requested by a service.

disk_size_in_gib.description: Root disk size in GiB for nodes provisioned by Karpenter (e.g., `50`).

enabled.description: Whether to enforce resource limits on the default node pool.

max_cpu_in_vcpu.description: Maximum total vCPU cores that Karpenter can provision for the default node pool.

max_memory_in_gibibytes.description: Maximum total memory in GiB that Karpenter can provision for the default node pool.

limits.description: Resource limits for the default node pool. Use this to cap the total resources Karpenter can provision for application workloads.

default_override.description: Override options for the Qovery **default** node pool. The default node pool runs user application workloads. Use this to set resource limits.

key.description:
The requirement key. Valid values:

  - `InstanceFamily` - EC2 instance family (e.g., `c5`, `m5`, `t3a`). Use broad families to reduce allocation issues.
  - `InstanceSize` - EC2 instance size (e.g., `small`, `medium`, `xlarge`, `2xlarge`).
  - `Arch` - CPU architecture (e.g., `AMD64`, `ARM64`).

operator.description: The operator for the requirement. Currently only `In` is supported, meaning the node must match one of the specified values.

values.description: List of allowed values for the requirement. For example, for `InstanceFamily`: `["c5", "m5", "t3a"]`, for `Arch`: `["AMD64", "ARM64"]`.

requirements.description: List of node selection requirements for the Karpenter node pool. Each requirement constrains which EC2 instances Karpenter can provision. You should define at least `InstanceFamily`, `InstanceSize`, and `Arch` requirements.

days.description: List of days of the week when consolidation should run (e.g., `["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday"]`).

duration.description: Duration of the consolidation window. Must follow the ISO-8601 duration format: `PThhHmmM` (e.g., `PT04H00M` for a 4-hour window).

enabled.description: Whether the consolidation schedule defined here is active. Set to `true` to enable scheduled consolidation.

start_time.description: Start time for the consolidation window. Must follow the ISO-8601 time format: `PThh:mm` (e.g., `PT02:00` for 2:00 AM UTC).

consolidation.description: Node consolidation schedule for the stable node pool. Consolidation replaces underutilized nodes with more cost-effective alternatives. By default, no consolidation occurs on stable nodes.

enabled.description: Whether to enforce resource limits on the stable node pool.

max_cpu_in_vcpu.description: Maximum total vCPU cores that Karpenter can provision for the stable node pool.

max_memory_in_gibibytes.description: Maximum total memory in GiB that Karpenter can provision for the stable node pool.

limits.description: Resource limits for the stable node pool. Use this to cap the total resources Karpenter can provision for stable workloads.

stable_override.description: Override options for the Qovery **stable** node pool. The stable node pool runs services that require consistent availability (e.g., Qovery agents). Use this to configure consolidation windows and resource limits.

qovery_node_pools.description: Karpenter node pool configuration. Defines the requirements (instance families, sizes, architectures) and optional resource limits for Qovery-managed node pools.

spot_enabled.description: Whether to enable EC2 Spot instances for cost savings. Spot instances can be interrupted by AWS with a 2-minute notice, so enable this only for fault-tolerant workloads.

karpenter.description: Karpenter configuration for AWS EKS clusters. [Karpenter](https://karpenter.sh/) is a Kubernetes node autoscaler that automatically provisions right-sized compute resources. When Karpenter is enabled, do not set `instance_type`, `min_running_nodes`, or `max_running_nodes` — Karpenter manages node scaling automatically.

static_ips_count.description: Number of static IPs to allocate for GCP NAT gateways. Must be greater than or equal to `1`. Meaningful only when `static_ips_enabled` is `true`. Default: `1`.

static_ips_enabled.description: Whether to reserve static egress IPs for the GCP NAT gateways. Default: `false` (ephemeral egress IPs).

nat_gateways.description:
GCP NAT Gateway static egress IP configuration. Reserved static egress IPs are an explicit opt-in via `static_ips_enabled = true` (requires `static_ip = true`).

Omitting this block or setting `static_ips_enabled = false` keeps the platform default (ephemeral egress IPs).

Removing this block after it was enabled resets to disabled with a visible diff on the next plan.

~> **Note:** This block is ignored on non-GCP clusters; only the default value `{static_ips_enabled=false, static_ips_count=1}` is accepted in those cases.

static_ip.description:
Whether to assign static IP addresses to the cluster nodes or NAT gateways. Useful when your services need to be allowlisted by IP. Default: `false`.

~> **Warning:** This value cannot be changed once the cluster has been deployed — the API rejects the change. Destroy and recreate the cluster to change it. On GCP, reserved static egress IPs are toggled via `nat_gateways.static_ips_enabled`, which remains editable after deployment.

vpc_subnet.description:
Custom VPC CIDR block for non-GCP clusters. This defines the IP address range for the entire VPC. Default: `10.0.0.0/16`.

~> **Note:** This value is ignored for GCP clusters unless a non-default value is configured, which is rejected because GCP uses its own network configuration.

~> **Warning:** This value cannot be changed after cluster creation. Changing it will require destroying and recreating the cluster.

features.description: Optional cluster features configuration. Use this block to customize VPC settings, enable static IPs, deploy on an existing VPC (AWS or GCP), or enable Karpenter for AWS clusters.

id.description: Unique identifier of the cluster (UUID format).

kubernetes_namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace where cert-manager is installed (e.g., `cert-manager` or `qovery`).

cert_manager_parameters.description: Configuration for cert-manager, used for automatic TLS certificate provisioning.

enabled.description: Enable or disable EKS Anywhere cluster backup.

bucket.description: S3 bucket name used to store EKS Anywhere backup artifacts.

key_prefix.description: Optional S3 key prefix used for backup object keys.

region.description: AWS region where the backup bucket is hosted.

role_arn.description: IAM role ARN assumed to upload backup artifacts.

s3.description: S3 settings used to store backup artifacts.

cluster_backup.description: Backup settings for EKS Anywhere clusters.

branch.description: Repository branch name. Defaults to the repository default branch when omitted.

commit_id.description: Optional git commit SHA to pin EKS Anywhere configuration to a specific revision. If omitted, the latest commit from the selected branch is used.

git_token_id.description: Qovery Git token ID used to access the repository.

url.description: Git repository URL containing the EKS Anywhere YAML files.

git_repository.description: Git repository settings used by Qovery to read and update EKS Anywhere configuration.

yaml_file_path.description: Path to the EKS Anywhere cluster YAML file in the Git repository (for example: `clusters/prod/cluster.yaml`).

eks_anywhere_parameters.description: Configuration for EKS Anywhere GitOps integration. Use this block to declare the Git repository and YAML path used for EKS Anywhere cluster lifecycle.

ip_address_pools.description: List of IP address pools for MetalLB. Each entry can be a single IP or an IP range (e.g., `192.168.1.100` or `192.168.1.100-192.168.1.200`). These IPs must be routable on your network.

metal_lb_parameters.description: Configuration for MetalLB, a bare-metal load balancer for Kubernetes. Required for `PARTIALLY_MANAGED` clusters to expose services externally.

annotation_external_dns_kubernetes_targe.description: IP address or hostname used by external-dns for DNS record creation (e.g., `192.168.1.100`).

annotation_metal_lb_load_balancer_ips.description: IP address annotation for MetalLB load balancer allocation (e.g., `192.168.1.100`). Must be within a MetalLB IP address pool.

default_ssl_certificate.description: Default SSL certificate reference in `namespace/secret-name` format (e.g., `qovery/letsencrypt-acme-qovery-cert`).

publish_status_address.description: Public IP address reported in the ingress status. This is the IP that external DNS will resolve to.

replica_count.description: Number of Nginx ingress controller replicas. Increase for high-availability setups.

nginx_parameters.description: Configuration for the Nginx ingress controller deployed on the cluster.

infrastructure_charts_parameters.description: Infrastructure Helm chart parameters for `PARTIALLY_MANAGED` (EKS Anywhere) clusters. **Required** when `kubernetes_mode` is `PARTIALLY_MANAGED`. These configure the core infrastructure components (ingress, TLS, load balancing) on your on-premise cluster.

cluster_arn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the EKS cluster. Only populated for AWS clusters after deployment.

cluster_name.description: The name of the Kubernetes cluster as assigned by the cloud provider. Available after deployment for all providers.

cluster_oidc_issuer.description: The OIDC issuer URL for the cluster. Useful for configuring IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA on AWS, workload identity on Azure). Available for AWS and Azure after deployment.

cluster_self_link.description: The self-link URL of the GKE cluster. Only populated for GCP clusters after deployment.

vpc_id.description: The VPC ID used by the cluster. Only populated for AWS clusters after deployment. Useful for setting up VPC peering or other networking resources.

infrastructure_outputs.description: Read-only outputs from the underlying Kubernetes infrastructure. These values are populated after the cluster is deployed and can be used to integrate with other infrastructure resources.

instance_type.description:
Instance type for the cluster nodes. The available values depend on the cloud provider:

  - **AWS**: EC2 instance types (e.g., `t3a.xlarge`, `m5.large`). Not required when Karpenter is enabled.
  - **GCP**: Machine types or `AUTO_PILOT` for GKE Autopilot mode.
  - **Scaleway**: Node types (e.g., `DEV1-L`, `GP1-S`).
  - **Azure**: VM sizes (e.g., `Standard_B2s_v2`, `Standard_D4s_v3`).

enabled.description: Whether the KEDA operator is installed on the cluster. Default: `false`.

keda.description: Optional KEDA configuration. KEDA ([Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling](https://keda.sh/)) installs the KEDA operator on the cluster, which unlocks event-driven autoscaling (including scale-to-zero) for services. Toggling this triggers a cluster redeploy.

kubeconfig.description: Kubeconfig YAML content for connecting to the cluster. **Required** for `PARTIALLY_MANAGED` (EKS Anywhere) clusters. This is a sensitive value and will not be displayed in plan output. Use `file()` to read from a file.

kubernetes_mode.description:
Kubernetes management mode for the cluster. Default: `MANAGED`.

  - `MANAGED` - Fully managed Kubernetes cluster provisioned and managed by Qovery (e.g., AWS EKS, GCP GKE, Azure AKS).
  - `SELF_MANAGED` - Bring your own Kubernetes cluster. Qovery deploys workloads but does not manage infrastructure.
  - `PARTIALLY_MANAGED` - EKS Anywhere / on-premise mode. Qovery manages workloads on a user-provided Kubernetes cluster via kubeconfig. Requires `kubeconfig` and `infrastructure_charts_parameters`.

labels_group_ids.description: List of labels group ids. Labels groups allow you to add Kubernetes labels to the cluster's resources. **Currently supported only for EKS (AWS managed Kubernetes) clusters.** See [Labels & Annotations](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/labels-annotations).

max_running_nodes.description:
Maximum number of nodes the cluster autoscaler can scale up to. Must be `>= 1`. Default: `10`.

~> **Note:** Must be set to `1` for K3S clusters. Do not set this attribute when Karpenter is enabled (Karpenter manages scaling automatically).

min_running_nodes.description:
Minimum number of nodes running for the cluster autoscaler. Must be `>= 1`. Default: `3`.

~> **Note:** Must be set to `1` for K3S clusters. Do not set this attribute when Karpenter is enabled (Karpenter manages scaling automatically).

name.description: Name of the cluster. Must be unique within the organization.

organization_id.description: ID of the Qovery organization in which to create the cluster. **Cannot be changed after creation** (forces resource replacement).

production.description: Flag to mark this cluster as a production cluster. Production clusters may have different default settings and safeguards. Default: `false`.

region.description: Cloud provider region where the cluster will be deployed (e.g., `us-east-2` for AWS, `europe-west9` for GCP, `pl-waw-1` for Scaleway, `westeurope` for Azure). For PARTIALLY_MANAGED clusters, use `on-premise`.

description.description: Human-readable description of the route's purpose.

destination.description: Destination CIDR block for the route (e.g., `10.1.0.0/16`).

target.description: Target gateway or endpoint for the route (e.g., a VPC peering connection ID or NAT gateway ID).

routing_table.description: Custom routing table entries for the cluster VPC. Use this to define network routes for traffic between the cluster and other networks (e.g., VPN, peering connections).

access_key.description: AWS access key ID. Required when type is AWS_STATIC_CREDENTIALS.

json_credentials.description: GCP service account JSON credentials. Required when type is GCP_JSON_CREDENTIALS.

region.description: AWS region. Required when type is AWS_STATIC_CREDENTIALS.

role_arn.description: IAM role ARN. Required when type is AWS_ROLE_ARN.

secret_key.description: AWS secret access key. Required when type is AWS_STATIC_CREDENTIALS.

type.description: Authentication mode. One of: AUTOMATICALLY_CONFIGURED, AWS_ROLE_ARN, AWS_STATIC_CREDENTIALS, GCP_JSON_CREDENTIALS.

authentication.description: Authentication configuration for the secret manager.

project_id.description: GCP project ID. Required when type is GCP_SECRET_MANAGER.

region.description: Region of the secret manager endpoint.

type.description: Type of secret manager endpoint. One of: AWS_PARAMETER_STORE, AWS_SECRET_MANAGER, GCP_SECRET_MANAGER.

endpoint.description: Endpoint configuration for the secret manager.

id.description: Id of the secret manager access.

name.description: Name of the secret manager access.

secret_manager_accesses.description: List of external secret manager configurations for the cluster. Each entry grants the cluster access to a secret provider (AWS Parameter Store, AWS Secrets Manager, or GCP Secret Manager).

state.description:
Desired state of the cluster. Default: `DEPLOYED`.

  - `DEPLOYED` - The cluster is running and ready to accept workloads.
  - `STOPPED` - The cluster infrastructure is stopped to save costs. All workloads will be unavailable.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery cluster resource. This is used to create and manage Kubernetes clusters on your chosen cloud provider through Qovery.

Qovery supports clusters on **AWS** (EKS), **GCP** (GKE), **Scaleway** (Kapsule), and **Azure** (AKS). Each cloud provider requires its own credentials resource (e.g., `qovery_aws_credentials`). For AWS clusters, you can optionally enable **Karpenter** for automatic node provisioning or deploy on an **existing VPC**. For GCP clusters, you can use **Autopilot** mode or deploy on an **existing VPC**. AWS also supports **PARTIALLY_MANAGED** mode for EKS Anywhere on-premise clusters.

api_token.description: Cloudflare API token. This value must be provided on create and update and is not returned by the Qovery API.

cloudflare.description: Cloudflare DNS provider configuration. Required when `provider_type` is `CLOUDFLARE`.

cluster_id.description: Id of the cluster whose DNS provider is managed by this resource.

domain.description: DNS domain associated with the cluster.

id.description: Id of the cluster DNS provider resource. This is the cluster id.

aws_secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key. This value must be provided on create and update and is not returned by the Qovery API.

type.description: Route53 credentials type. Only `STATIC` is supported.

route53.description: Route53 DNS provider configuration. Required when `provider_type` is `ROUTE53`.

block.description: Provides a Qovery cluster DNS provider resource. Declare this resource only when Terraform must explicitly manage the cluster DNS provider.

advanced_settings_json.description: Advanced settings as JSON. Use `jsonencode()` to set values. Only include settings you want to override. Full list available in [Qovery API documentation](https://api-doc.qovery.com/#tag/Containers/operation/getDefaultContainerAdvancedSettings).

annotations_group_ids.description: List of annotations group ids. Annotations groups allow you to add Kubernetes annotations to the container's pods.

arguments.description: List of arguments of this container. Overrides the Docker image's default `CMD`.

auto_deploy.description: Specify if the container will be automatically redeployed after receiving a new image tag from the container registry.

auto_preview.description: Specify if the environment preview option is activated or not for this container. When enabled, Qovery creates a preview environment for each pull request.

cooldown_period_seconds.description: Period in seconds to wait after the last trigger before scaling back down. Defaults to 300.

polling_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds between each KEDA polling of the scalers. Defaults to 30.

config_json.description: Scaler configuration as JSON. Mutually exclusive with config_yaml.

config_yaml.description: Scaler configuration as raw YAML. Mutually exclusive with config_json.

enabled.description: Whether the scaler is enabled. Defaults to true.

role.description: Role of the scaler: PRIMARY or SAFETY.

scaler_type.description: Type of the KEDA scaler (e.g. cpu, memory, prometheus, cron).

trigger_authentication.description: Inline KEDA TriggerAuthentication for this scaler.

scalers.description: List of KEDA scalers driving the autoscaling. At least one scaler is required.

autoscaling.description: Event-driven autoscaling (KEDA) configuration. KEDA is additive to the CPU/memory HPA (min/max_running_instances) and unlocks scale-to-zero (min_running_instances = 0). Requires KEDA to be enabled on the cluster.

value.description: Value of the environment variable.

built_in_environment_variables.description: List of built-in environment variables linked to this container. Built-in variables are automatically generated by Qovery and include host information, port mappings, and other service metadata. These are read-only and cannot be modified.

cpu.description: CPU of the container in millicores (m) [1000m = 1 CPU].

generate_certificate.description: Qovery will generate and manage a TLS/SSL certificate for this domain using Let's Encrypt.

use_cdn.description:
Indicates if the custom domain is behind a CDN (e.g. Cloudflare). This affects how Qovery validates the CNAME during deployment:
  - If `true`: Qovery only checks that the domain points to an IP.
  - If `false`: Qovery checks that the domain resolves to the correct service Load Balancer.

validation_domain.description: URL provided by Qovery. You must create a CNAME on your DNS provider using that URL.

custom_domains.description: List of custom domains linked to this container. You must configure a CNAME record on your DNS provider pointing to the `validation_domain` value.

deployment_stage_id.description: Id of the deployment stage. Deployment stages allow you to control the order in which services are deployed within an environment.

entrypoint.description: Entrypoint of the container. Overrides the Docker image's default `ENTRYPOINT`.

environment_id.description: Id of the environment. Changing this forces the container to be re-created.

description.description: Description of the environment variable alias.

id.description: Id of the environment variable alias.

key.description: Name of the environment variable alias.

value.description: Name of the variable to alias.

environment_variable_aliases.description: List of environment variable aliases linked to this container. An alias creates a new environment variable name that references the value of an existing variable. The `key` is the alias name and `value` is the name of the variable being aliased.

description.description: Description of the environment variable file.

id.description: Id of the environment variable file.

key.description: Key of the environment variable file.

mount_path.description: Mount path of the environment variable file.

value.description: Value of the environment variable file.

environment_variable_files.description: List of environment variable files linked to this container.

description.description: Description of the environment variable override.

id.description: Id of the environment variable override.

key.description: Name of the environment variable override.

value.description: Value of the environment variable override.

environment_variable_overrides.description: List of environment variable overrides linked to this container. An override replaces the value of an existing environment variable defined at a higher scope (project or environment). The `key` must match the name of the variable to override.

value.description: Value of the environment variable.

environment_variables.description: List of environment variables linked to this container. Environment variables at the container level have the highest precedence and override variables set at the project or environment level.

ephemeral_storage.description: Ephemeral storage of the container in GiB. When unset, the platform default is used.

external_host.description: The container external FQDN host. Only available if your container has at least one publicly accessible port.

description.description: Description of the external secret file.

id.description: Id of the external secret file.

key.description: Name of the external secret file.

mount_path.description: Absolute path where the secret file will be mounted inside the container.

reference.description: Reference to the upstream secret (e.g. the secret name or ARN in AWS Secrets Manager).

secret_manager_access_id.description: Id of the secret manager access to use for this external secret file.

external_secret_files.description: List of external secret files linked to this container. External secret files reference upstream secrets (e.g. from AWS Secrets Manager) and are mounted as files at a given path inside the container.

reference.description: Reference to the upstream secret (e.g. the secret name or ARN in AWS Secrets Manager).

secret_manager_access_id.description: Id of the secret manager access to use for this external secret.

external_secrets.description: List of external secrets linked to this container. External secrets reference upstream secrets (e.g. from AWS Secrets Manager) via a secret manager access configuration.

failure_threshold.description: Number of consecutive failures required to declare the probe as failed.

initial_delay_seconds.description: Number of seconds to wait after the container starts before the first probe is executed. Use this to give your application time to initialize.

period_seconds.description: How often (in seconds) to perform the probe after the initial delay.

success_threshold.description: Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure.

timeout_seconds.description: Number of seconds after which the probe times out. If the probe does not respond within this time, it is considered failed.

command.description: The command and its arguments to execute (e.g. `["cat", "/tmp/healthy"]`).

exec.description: Exec probe: runs a command inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0. The command binary must be present in the container image.

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

service.description: The gRPC service name to health-check. If not specified, the overall server health is checked.

grpc.description: gRPC probe: checks that the given port responds to gRPC health check requests. The service must implement the [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/10/01/health-checking-grpc-servers-on-kubernetes/#introducing-grpc-health-probe).

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

scheme.description: Scheme to use for the HTTP request. Must be `HTTP` or `HTTPS`.

host.description: Optional host to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

tcp.description: TCP probe: checks that a TCP connection can be established on the given port.

type.description: Kind of check to run for this probe. Exactly one of `tcp`, `http`, `grpc`, or `exec` must be configured.

liveness_probe.description: Configuration for the liveness probe, used to determine when your service is working correctly. If the liveness probe fails, the service container is killed and restarted.

service.description: The gRPC service name to health-check. If not specified, the overall server health is checked.

grpc.description: gRPC probe: checks that the given port responds to gRPC health check requests. The service must implement the [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/10/01/health-checking-grpc-servers-on-kubernetes/#introducing-grpc-health-probe).

path.description: The path for the HTTP GET request (e.g. `/health`, `/ready`). Defaults to `/`.

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

scheme.description: Scheme to use for the HTTP request. Must be `HTTP` or `HTTPS`.

host.description: Optional host to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

port.description: The port number to try to connect to.

tcp.description: TCP probe: checks that a TCP connection can be established on the given port.

type.description: Kind of check to run for this probe. Exactly one of `tcp`, `http`, `grpc`, or `exec` must be configured.

readiness_probe.description: Configuration for the readiness probe, used to determine when your service is ready to receive traffic. If the readiness probe fails, the service is temporarily removed from the load balancer until it passes again.

healthchecks.description: Configuration for the healthchecks that are going to be executed against your service. At least one of `readiness_probe` or `liveness_probe` should be configured for production workloads.

icon_uri.description: Icon URI representing the container. Used in the Qovery console UI.

image_name.description: Name of the container image (e.g. `nginx`, `my-org/my-app`). Do not include the tag.

internal_host.description: The container internal host. Use this to communicate between services within the same environment.

is_skipped.description: If true, the service is excluded from environment-level bulk deployments while remaining assigned to its deployment stage.

labels_group_ids.description: List of labels group ids. Labels groups allow you to add Kubernetes labels to the container's pods.

max_running_instances.description: Maximum number of instances running for the container.

memory.description: RAM of the container in MB [1024MB = 1GB].

min_running_instances.description: Minimum number of instances running for the container.

external_port.description: External port of the container. Required if `ports.publicly_accessible = true`. Must be between 1 and 65535.

internal_port.description: Internal port of the container. Must be between 1 and 65535.

is_default.description: If this port will be used for the root domain. The API may override this value based on port configuration (e.g., when only one publicly accessible port exists, it will be set as default).

protocol.description: Protocol used for the port of the container.

publicly_accessible.description: Specify if the port is exposed to the world or not for this container.

ports.description: List of ports linked to this container. At least one port must be set as `publicly_accessible = true` with an `external_port` for the container to be reachable from the internet.

registry_id.description: Id of the container registry (from `qovery_container_registry`) that stores the Docker image for this container.

value.description: Name of the secret to alias.

secret_aliases.description: List of secret aliases linked to this container. An alias creates a new secret name that references the value of an existing secret. The `key` is the alias name and `value` is the name of the secret being aliased.

mount_path.description: Mount path of the secret file.

value.description: Value of the secret file.

secret_files.description: List of secret files linked to this container.

value.description: Value of the secret override. The value is write-only and will not be displayed in plan outputs.

secret_overrides.description: List of secret overrides linked to this container. An override replaces the value of an existing secret defined at a higher scope (project or environment). The `key` must match the name of the secret to override.

value.description: Value of the secret. The value is write-only and will not be displayed in plan outputs.

secrets.description: List of secrets linked to this container. Secrets behave like environment variables but their values are stored securely and not visible in plan outputs.

mount_point.description: Mount point of the storage for the container.

size.description: Size of the storage for the container in GB [1024MB = 1GB].

type.description: Type of the storage for the container.

storage.description: List of persistent storage volumes linked to this container. Data stored in these volumes persists across container restarts.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery container resource. This can be used to create and manage Qovery containers.

A container is a service that runs a Docker image from a container registry within a Qovery environment. Unlike applications (which are built from source code), containers use pre-built images.

access_key_id.description: AWS Access Key ID. Required if `kind` is `ECR` or `PUBLIC_ECR`.

json_credentials.description: GCP service account JSON key used to authenticate with the registry. Required if `kind` is `GCP_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY`.

password.description: Password or access token for authentication. Required if `kind` is `DOCKER_HUB`, `GITHUB_CR`, `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_CR`, `GITLAB_CR`, or `GENERIC_CR`.

region.description: Region of the registry. Required if `kind` is `ECR`, `SCALEWAY_CR` or `GCP_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY` (e.g. `us-east-1`, `fr-par`).

scaleway_access_key.description: Scaleway Access Key. Required if `kind` is `SCALEWAY_CR`.

scaleway_project_id.description: Scaleway Project ID. Required if `kind` is `SCALEWAY_CR`.

scaleway_secret_key.description: Scaleway Secret Key. Required if `kind` is `SCALEWAY_CR`.

secret_access_key.description: AWS Secret Access Key. Required if `kind` is `ECR` or `PUBLIC_ECR`.

username.description: Username for authentication. Required if `kind` is `DOCKER_HUB`, `GITHUB_CR`, `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_CR`, `GITLAB_CR`, or `GENERIC_CR`.

config.description: Configuration needed to authenticate with the container registry. Required fields depend on the `kind` of registry.

kind.description:
Kind of the container registry. Supported values:
  - `ECR`: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (private).
  - `PUBLIC_ECR`: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (public).
  - `DOCR`: DigitalOcean Container Registry.
  - `SCALEWAY_CR`: Scaleway Container Registry.
  - `DOCKER_HUB`: Docker Hub.
  - `GITHUB_CR`: GitHub Container Registry.
  - `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_CR`: GitHub Enterprise Container Registry.
  - `GITLAB_CR`: GitLab Container Registry.
  - `GCP_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY`: Google Cloud Artifact Registry.
  - `AZURE_CR`: Azure Container Registry.
  - `GENERIC_CR`: Any OCI-compatible container registry.

organization_id.description: Id of the organization. **Cannot be changed after creation** (forces resource replacement).

url.description: URL of the container registry (e.g. `https://docker.io` for Docker Hub, `https://<account_id>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com` for ECR).

block.description:
Provides a Qovery container registry resource. This can be used to create and manage Qovery container registries.

A container registry stores Docker images that can be deployed as Qovery container services. Container registries are configured at the organization level and can be referenced by containers across all projects.

accessibility.description:
Accessibility of the database.
  - `PUBLIC`: Database is accessible from outside the cluster.
  - `PRIVATE`: Database is only accessible from services within the same environment.

Default: `PUBLIC`.

annotations_group_ids.description: List of annotations group ids. Annotations groups allow you to add Kubernetes annotations to the database pods (only for `CONTAINER` mode).

cpu.description: CPU of the database in millicores (m) [1000m = 1 CPU]. Only applicable when `mode = "CONTAINER"`. Ignored for `MANAGED` mode (use `instance_type` instead).

deployment_stage_id.description: Id of the deployment stage. Deployment stages allow you to control the order in which services are deployed within an environment.

environment_id.description: Id of the environment. Changing this forces the database to be re-created.

external_host.description: The database external FQDN host. Only available when `accessibility = "PUBLIC"`.

icon_uri.description: Icon URI representing the database. Used in the Qovery console UI.

instance_type.description: Instance type of the database. Required when `mode = "MANAGED"`. Not applicable for `CONTAINER` mode. The available instance types depend on your cloud provider (e.g. `db.t3.micro` for AWS RDS).

internal_host.description: The database internal host. Use this to connect from services within the same environment (recommended over external host).

is_skipped.description: If true, the service is excluded from environment-level bulk deployments while remaining assigned to its deployment stage.

labels_group_ids.description: List of labels group ids. Labels groups allow you to add Kubernetes labels to the database pods (only for `CONTAINER` mode).

login.description: The login (username) to connect to your database. Automatically generated by Qovery.

memory.description: RAM of the database in MB [1024MB = 1GB]. Only applicable when `mode = "CONTAINER"`. Ignored for `MANAGED` mode (use `instance_type` instead).

mode.description:
Mode of the database. Cannot be updated after creation.
  - `CONTAINER`: Runs the database in a container on your cluster. You can configure `cpu` and `memory`. Suitable for development and staging.
  - `MANAGED`: Uses your cloud provider's managed database service (e.g. AWS RDS). You must configure `instance_type` instead of `cpu`/`memory`. Recommended for production.

password.description: The password to connect to your database. Automatically generated by Qovery.

port.description: The port number to connect to your database. Automatically assigned by Qovery based on the database type.

storage.description: Storage of the database in GB [1024MB = 1GB]. Cannot be updated after creation.

type.description:
Type of the database engine. Cannot be updated after creation.
  - `POSTGRESQL`: PostgreSQL relational database.
  - `MYSQL`: MySQL relational database.
  - `MONGODB`: MongoDB document database.
  - `REDIS`: Redis in-memory data store.

version.description: Version of the database engine (e.g. `14` for PostgreSQL 14, `8.0` for MySQL 8.0). Available versions depend on the `type` and `mode` chosen. Refer to Qovery documentation for supported versions per database type.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery database resource. This can be used to create and manage Qovery databases.

Databases can run in two modes:
  - `CONTAINER`: Runs the database engine in a container on your cluster (suitable for development/staging).
  - `MANAGED`: Uses your cloud provider's managed database service (e.g. AWS RDS, recommended for production).

desired_state.description:
Desired state of the deployment. Setting this to `RUNNING` starts all services, `STOPPED` stops all services, and `RESTARTED` triggers a restart of all running services.
	- Can be: `RESTARTED`, `RUNNING`, `STOPPED`.

environment_id.description: Identifier of the environment to deploy (UUID format).

id.description: Unique identifier of the deployment (UUID format). If not provided, a random UUID will be generated.

version.description: Version identifier to force a redeployment when `desired_state` hasn't changed. Use a random UUID (e.g., via `uuid()`) to force Terraform to trigger a new deployment on every apply.

block.description:
Provides a Qovery deployment resource. This is used to trigger and manage the deployment state of an environment and all its services.

~> **Note:** This resource does not support import. When destroying this resource, all services in the environment will be stopped.

environment_id.description: Identifier of the environment for this deployment stage (UUID format). **Cannot be changed after creation** (forces resource replacement).

id.description: Unique identifier of the deployment stage (UUID format).

is_after.description: Identifier (UUID) of another deployment stage. Positions this stage immediately after the specified stage in the deployment order.

is_before.description: Identifier (UUID) of another deployment stage. Positions this stage immediately before the specified stage in the deployment order.

block.description:
